evidence.snippet: Nanexa AB (Nasdaq First North Growth Market: NANEXA), Uppsala, Sweden, granted Moderna a license and option agreement for PharmaShell-based products: USD 3 million upfront, up to USD 500 million in development/commercial milestones plus tiered royalties. PharmaShell uses atomic layer deposition (ALD) to coat drug particles for tailored, long-acting (1-3 month) release, terminal sterilization, and room-temperature stability. Release notes existing collaboration agreements with Novo Nordisk and AstraZeneca.
Moderna taps Nanexa to improve delivery of injectable therapies in a back-loaded $500M pact, to develop long-acting versions of Moderna's mRNA-based compounds.

Samchundang has four LAI products nearing commercialization (two microsphere-, two liposome-based, in development since 2017). Octreotide (acromegaly) monthly microsphere formulation is in final clinical stage with 2026 FDA submission targeted; US and Canada supply/partner contracts already signed. Leuprorelin (prostate cancer) has a four-interval lineup (1/3/4/6-month) with particle size matched to the originator (23-gauge needle compatible) and commercial-scale batches validated (3,000/6,000/10,000 units); a partner has requested a term sheet.

G2GBio (existing tracked umbrella samsung-bioepis-g2gbio-gb7001) and SpiderCore, a KAIST-founded AI deep-tech startup, signed a contract to build an agentic-AI R&D platform for long-acting injectable microparticle development -- integrating G2GBio's internal research data with public literature/patents to auto-propose formulation and process conditions, targeting 2x faster development and 50% lower cost within two years, eventually extending to G2GBio's CDMO business.

Alveus Therapeutics (Philadelphia/Copenhagen), incubated by New Rhein Healthcare Investors, launched with $159.8M Series A (New Rhein, Andera Partners, Omega Funds, Sanofi Capital, Kurma Partners, Avego BioScience Capital). Lead candidate ALV-100 is a fusion protein activating GLP-1 while blocking GIP, engineered for durability with a quarterly-dosing target (vs. monthly for Amgen's MariTide). Pipeline also includes ALV-200, a peptide selectively activating amylin receptor 3 for satiety/lean-mass preservation, planned for clinical entry mid-2027.

Phase 2/3 open-label study (NCT07722728) evaluating PK, safety and tolerability of B2227 Extended-Release Injectable Suspension (subcutaneous, single-dose 30/70/150 mg) versus Vraylar (cariprazine) in schizophrenia patients; lead sponsor is Bostal Drug Delivery Co., Ltd. First posted 2026-07-23.

CSPC Pharmaceutical Group received US FDA clearance to begin US clinical trials of SYHX2008, a once-monthly long-acting octreotide injection for acromegaly and gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, designed for subcutaneous self-administration; already in Phase III trials in China against existing octreotide microsphere products. Dated June 19, 2026.

Phase 1 sequential-dose-cohort PK/safety study (NCT07269873) of BICX104, a subcutaneous implantable biodegradable naltrexone pellet (997.5 mg NTX base anhydrous, target ≥1 ng/mL for 3 months) with or without bupropion, compared to Vivitrol (naltrexone IM depot injection); lead sponsor BioCorRx Pharmaceuticals Inc. First posted 2025-12-08.

BioCorRx Inc. (OTCQB: BICX) submitted an FDA expanded-access application for BICX104, a biodegradable long-acting subcutaneous naltrexone pellet delivering therapeutic levels for 84 days — three times the duration of the 28-day marketed Vivitrol depot injection. Dated August 15, 2023.

Mapi Pharma announced initial Phase I/IIa clinical results supporting continued development of a once-monthly Cariprazine Depot (an atypical-antipsychotic long-acting injectable), a third distinct LAI depot asset from Mapi Pharma alongside its already-tracked GA Depot (glatiramer acetate) and Semaglutide Depot programs. No dedicated umbrella file currently covers this asset.

US11,931,357 (issued 2024-03-19) and US12,251,380, both assigned to Mapi Pharma Ltd. and filed 2023-02-14 (claiming benefit of a provisional filed 2022-03-17), claim depot systems (in-situ implant, subcutaneous/IM) providing prolonged release of active agent for at least 4 weeks, dosed roughly monthly to quarterly -- corroborating patent-level evidence for the once-monthly Cariprazine Depot program. Found via weekly patent sweep.

source.name: Technical University of Denmark (DTU) official news page

evidence.snippet: "A surgical strike in the battle against infections" (dtu.dk, May 2026): Precision Antibiotics, a DTU spinout, is developing an injectable drug depot (product family referenced elsewhere as 'CarboCell G/C') delivering a combination of two existing antibiotics (gentamicin + clindamycin) locally into bone/soft tissue after e.g. a bone fracture, sustaining high local concentrations over several weeks to address biofilm infections resistant to systemic treatment. Raised DKK 60 million (~$8-9M) to fund first-in-human Phase 1 trials expected to start 2027. Related to a Novo Nordisk Foundation grant referencing 'CarboCell AntiBiotics (CCAB)', led by Anders Elias Hansen at DTU. Direct fetch of dtu.dk was EGRESS_BLOCKED this run; content is from search-engine snippet only, not independently re-verified by full-page read. SCOPE CAVEAT FOR REVIEWER: this is a local antibiotic depot for post-fracture bone/soft-tissue infection, not a systemic chronic-disease LAI (not GLP-1/antipsychotic/hormone-class) -- fits 'depot drug delivery tech' broadly but sits at the edge of the tracker's usual peptide/protein-LAI focus, flagging for a scope call rather than assuming inclusion.

Beijing-based QL Biopharm raised over RMB 500M (~$72M) in a Series C led by OrbiMed (with 5Y Capital, Apricot Capital, Huagai Capital, Qiming Venture Partners, TigerYeah Capital, Lanchi Ventures, TF Capital), announced March 2, 2026. Lead candidate zovaglutide (ZT002) is a GLP-1 receptor agonist injection designed for monthly dosing -- potentially the first monthly GLP-1 peptide to reach market -- now in a China Phase 3 obesity trial (first patient dosed January 2026) after Phase II data showed 13.8% weight loss by week 24 without reaching a plateau.

GSK is advancing felcorekibart, a long-acting engineered antibody originally developed by a China-founded biotech GSK acquired roughly two years ago, registering 6 new Phase 3 trials (2 COPD, 2 asthma, 2 CRSwNP). Corroborated by a TipRanks wire piece on the same COPD Phase 3 program. SCOPE CAVEAT FOR REVIEWER: this is a half-life-extended monoclonal antibody for respiratory disease (COPD/asthma/CRSwNP), not a depot/microsphere/peptide-LAI in the tracker's usual sense. It fits the 'molecular_engineering' technology_family loosely (durability via protein engineering, same broad category as GX-H9's hyFc or Metsera's engineered peptide) but is a therapeutic-area outlier versus the rest of the registry -- flagging for an explicit in/out-of-scope call rather than assuming inclusion.

AstraZeneca announced Jan 30, 2026 it will receive exclusive global rights outside China to CSPC's once-monthly injectable weight-management portfolio: lead clinical-ready asset SYH2082, a long-acting GLP-1R/GIPR agonist entering Phase I, plus three preclinical programmes, built on CSPC's AI-driven peptide discovery platform and proprietary 'LiquidGel' once-monthly dosing technology. CSPC receives $1.2B upfront plus up to $3.5B in development/regulatory milestones (plus commercial milestones/royalties); CSPC leads development through Phase I for all four programmes, then AstraZeneca takes over ex-China development/commercialization. CSPC retains China/Taiwan/HK/Macau rights with an AZ co-commercialization option post-approval. Deal expected to close Q2 2026. NOTE FOR REVIEWER: CSPC already has a separate pending candidate in this pipeline (cand-2026-09-02-007, CSPC ZhongQi Pharmaceutical Technology / SYHX2008, a long-acting octreotide for acromegaly) -- this is a different asset/subsidiary of the same corporate parent, surfaced independently via this run's wire skim, not a duplicate of that entry.

Corroborates deal terms: AstraZeneca signs deal worth up to $4.7bn total ($1.2B upfront + up to $3.5B milestones) with CSPC for once-monthly GLP-1R/GIPR agonist SYH2082 and three preclinical obesity/metabolic programmes.

evidence.snippet: Peer-reviewed report of long-acting hydrogel-based depot formulations of tirzepatide and semaglutide. The PNP hydrogel uses hydrophobically modified HPMC-C12 with PEG-PLA nanoparticles; a single injection sustained exposure over 42 days in animals, which the authors map to a once-every-four-months human therapy. Appel Sauce Studios LLC holds a global exclusive licence to the Stanford technology and a named inventor is a co-founder and advisor. Corporate footprint not yet independently verified: no company pipeline page, financing or clinical registration found this sweep.

Ribupatide (HRS9531) is a GLP-1/GIP dual receptor agonist with positive Phase 2 obesity data at 1, 2 and 4mg and an NMPA filing accepted in China for long-term weight management; partnered outside Greater China with Kailera Therapeutics as KAI-9531. FLAGGED FOR REVIEWER: surfaced while checking a secondary claim that Hengrui was developing monthly formulations, which this sweep could NOT confirm. Every source found describes once-weekly subcutaneous injection plus a once-daily oral tablet, so on current evidence this does not meet the long-acting-injectable bar and is queued for an explicit reject-with-reason rather than promotion.
